newsitem.title: GERMANY: German September M3 growth slows to 8.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: German September M3 growth slows to 8.4 pct.

text.p: German M3 money supply, the Bundesbank's key policy indicator, grew at a slower pace in September measuring 8.4 percent, the Bundesbank said on Monday.
More lively investment in securities and weaker lending to the private sector helped growth slow in September after it had unexpectedly ticked higher to 8.7 percent in August.
Analysts said the slowdown, while reassuring, would not prompt the central bank to nudge interest rates lower again in the near term. The number met market expectations.
"This does not raise expectations of further rate cuts," said Gerhard Grebe, chief economist at Bank Julius Baer in Frankfurt.
M3, which includes cash in circulation, time, sight and short term savings deposits, is a key policy guide for the Bundesbank because it foreshadows future inflation trends.
The Bundesbank has kept its main money market rate fixed at three percent since August. The discount rate remains at 2.5 percent while the Lombard rate is at 4.5 percent.
